h1: Do I need a building permit to replace windows in Newton, MA?
title: Newton Window Replacement Permits: Same-Size Units and Structural Changes
description: Check the difference between ordinary window replacement, structural opening changes, and historic district approval.
short_answer: The state building code exempts ordinary repairs, but a project that cuts or changes structural supports may require a building permit. Newton also requires historic review for window changes at properties in its Local Historic Districts. The exact permit treatment of a same-size replacement outside a historic area should be confirmed with ISD.

facts.text: The state code exempts ordinary repairs but requires a permit for specified structural work, including substantial cutting of structural members or removal of load-bearing support.
Newton's Local Historic District application process covers exterior changes. The city provides a specific window-replacement checklist for historic district applications.

qa.q: Can I change a window opening without checking for a permit?
qa.a: No. A change to the opening or its structural support may fall outside the ordinary-repair exemption. Confirm the plans with ISD before work begins.
